items.title: Blizzard Says Diablo 5 Was Too Big To Be A Diablo 4 Expansion
items.summary: Diablo 4 is far from dead, but don't expect any new expansions for the game going forward. Instead, Blizzard i

others.title: Blizzard Insists There Are 'Many Reasons to Keep Playing' Diablo 4 as Fans Debate End of Expansions and Diablo 5 in 2029

content.v: Diablo 4 is far from dead, but don't expect any new expansions for the game going forward. Instead, Blizzard is preparing to tell the darkest story yet in Diablo 5 , one that required a new numbered game to properly reintroduce Diablo himself back to the series, following his defeat in 2012's Diablo 3. Currently aiming for a 2029 release , this would mean that players are in for a relatively short wait for a new Diablo game--compared to previous releases--as Diablo 5 will arrive a mere six years after Diablo 4.

Speaking to GameSpot at BlizzCon , Diablo senior production director Tiffany Wat and executive producer Matt Zitterman explained that it made sense for Blizzard to move to a new Diablo so that the studio could make structural changes to the game--changes that would have been very challenging to pull off within the framework of a Diablo 4 expansion.

"It really started by looking at who our players are," Zitterman said. "Who are Diablo players? Why are they playing Diablo? What do they want out of a Diablo game? That is a really critical step in the early conceptual phase for a game, even before you're thinking about, like, 'Gosh, should we make this an expansion? Should we make it a sequel? How do we do this?' Looking at past examples, looking at what's working well in Diablo 4, where there are opportunities for improvement, and we kind of build our ambition for the game at the conceptual phase through those avenues of information."

"And as we started to understand and kind of solidify what that ambition was, it became very clear to us pretty early that in order to achieve what we wanted to achieve with this game, we needed to make some more deeply structural changes to the way the game works, changes that are just frankly hard to do in an expansion. Again, it's all about figuring out what the best way is to make the best Diablo game we can for players. Diablo is the main villain. Diablo is the guy that we want to tell a real story about. We want to tell a story that's on par with--and hopefully exceeds--the story we told with Lilith and Mephisto."
"And to do that in an expansion just didn't feel right. We needed to give him his own game."

Player feedback also plays a vital role in the development of Diablo 5, and Zitterman said that by announcing the game this early, Blizzard could make important changes well ahead of the game's eventual launch. "If we didn't announce now and we kind of held back until we were much further along in development, at that point, it's much harder to take that feedback and use it to make those really important changes and refinements to the game throughout development," Zitterman explained.

For more on Diablo 5, you can learn how combat could be even more ferocious , how the game will offer more character classes than ever , and how the Plague Knight uses the grossest powers to stay a step ahead of Diablo's demonic armies.

items.title: Valve had next-gen VR 'headsets ready three, four years ago and they were big, bulky devices' but went back to the drawing board after actually putting them on
items.summary: The versatile Steam Frame's focus is "on being lightweight and being comfortable".

others.title: Red Dead 2 Actor Shares A Gross Secret About The Game

content.v: The Steam Frame is here and it's one of the best VR headsets I've ever had attached to my face, just don't ask me about the price. But when we spoke to two of the people at Valve who helped create the device—Joy Lyons and Jeremy Selan—they told me the company actually had its new VR headsets ready years ago, but they made the tough decision to pull the plug on those designs.

"We had the headsets ready three, four years ago," Selan explains, "and they were big, bulky devices. They were more in the style of the Valve Index , and we put them on, and we're just like, this doesn't feel like what we would want the next round of our product to be."

We'd asked why now, why is this the right time to release a new VR headset? With sales dropping year over year and 2026 potentially being the worst year effectively since records began for PCVR releases, it doesn't necessarily seem like the perfect time to be putting out new virtual reality hardware, and that's before we even mention the memory and hardware pricing crisis.
"You asked, why now?" says Selan. "The answer with all Valve projects is 'as soon as we can'. Right, this was the soonest we could release the headset, but we had to make sure it was ready.

"The hardware engineers went back to the drawing board many, many times to finally achieve sort of the very small form factor, the comfortable, the lightweight. Figuring out all the system trade-offs with regards to power versus battery weight, versus cooling, and thermals. So this was absolutely the fastest we were capable of shipping the device that we were proud of.
"Now we thought that was going to be early 2026, and it turns out due to supply and component shortages and economics that in fact now was the soonest we could release it."

But it's not just about the hardware. As Valve engineer Joy Lyons notes, "The focus was on being lightweight and being comfortable", but while it's the hardware that makes that possible, all of the work Valve has been putting in with its previous releases on the software side have made this headset the one that actually gets released.

"We learned a lot with our portable systems," Lyons explains, "including the Steam Deck launch and all the work we did for emulation and the operating system, with Proton being able to run Windows-based games on Linux, on the SteamOS operating system.

"And so we've been continuing that work, and now we've got an ARM device, and so we think this is a great time to take advantage of Proton, being able to do FEX, which allows us to run x86 games on a piece of ARM hardware, and Lepton, which is the new work to do Android-based games, and have that work also on our SteamOS platform. And so we're able to have all these come together, as well as all of our work on the hardware side."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ipeAcTUdGYaexQjq5dvy7Q-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/JARYSgBLBsGsKWxePQJ3EP-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ctqTkWGv7gkcseWyqGetyS-1920-80.jpg

It's this kind of VR nexus point which has made the Steam Frame the right device for Valve, and at the right time. It is, of course, a PC VR device, with its almost uncanny ability to stream games wirelessly from your PC utterly seamlessly, but it is also a standalone device able to translate your x86 PC's Steam library and have that run inside an ARM-based VR headset. Again, almost seamlessly.

And then you also now have the ability to play Android games through Steam via the Lepton translation layer. Now, that's not just Candy Crush writ large on a massive virtual screen, this is specifically designed to capture the wealth of VR content released for the Meta Quest and its Android-based Horizon OS. And with this new world of potential content available to the Steam Frame as a portable device, it's been a bit of a journey of discovery even for Valve.

"I'm like, 'I wonder if this one will run?'" says Lyons. "And you download it, and you open it, and it runs, and you put it on the huge screen. That was the moment where it's just like, 'this is fun. I'm gonna take off my engineer hat. I'm gonna stop nitpicking every little thing that I know about the device, and I'll definitely address that tomorrow. But right now, I'm actually having fun.'
"I think I went through 89 games in a two week period… that's kind of the moment where it's like, 'yeah, this is great'."
"We're our own best testers," adds Selan. "So I do remember in those days I would have access to this secret prototype VR hardware, and I would take it home… and I'd still use my Steam Deck.

"And there became a transition point with this round of hardware, where when I took this home and this was my favorite device to use. And so, for me personally, that's when sort of a switch flipped in my head, and I was like, 'This is going to be a real thing'."

items.title: Wardogs Devs Are Watching Economy Cheaters Like Hawks
items.summary: With the FPS Wardogs dominating the Steam charts, developer Bulkhead is paying close attention to the game's v

content.v: With the FPS Wardogs dominating the Steam charts, developer Bulkhead is paying close attention to the game's various systems. The studio recently dropped a new patch that makes some necessary changes for server stability, while confirming that the team has their eyes on cheaters and exploiters.

As part of Patch 0.11 , which came out on September 14, Bulkhead announced that should any dogs of war take advantage of Wardogs' economy by farming servers, they'll find themselves either temporarily or permanently banned from the game.
"As an early access game, we’re not perfect, and we never will be," Bulkhead said in the patch notes. "But if you do find something and take advantage of it, we have decided to come down hard."
To be specific, Bulkhead outlined three different scenarios that will come with three different repercussions depending on the type of exploit you partake in.

Scenario 1: Stockpiling money by abusing cash exploits and bugs will result in a timed ban, with the length determined by whether you were banned previously. Your cash and experience will get reset, too.

Scenario 2: Showing economy exploits through tutorial content will be treated as "advertising cheats," resulting in a permanent ban. However, if you happen to stumble upon an exploit and share that with Bulkhead on Discord or social media, that'll be seen as an "alert," which prevents you from being permanently banned.
Scenario 3: If you're farming experience via server exploits, which Bulkhead says will result in "the most serious bans," your account will get banned permanently.
The studio clarified, though, that it's open to feedback on this policy, stating that these positions could change if enough people believe they're too harsh.

"In the very early stages of finding these issues you may find yourself getting away with it, but it doesn't take long for our backend data to flag abusers," Bulkhead said, "Effectively, if you find something and you then keep doing it, over and over again, that is abuse of an exploit. If you figure something out and test it once or twice, no biggy, thanks for helping us QA."

Wardogs is currently Steam's hottest game right now, with over 320,000 people playing at the time of writing. It didn't have the smoothest of starts , but the kinks are getting ironed out as the days go on. Players are a little riled up at the moment, though, particularly because people don't know how to close the door behind them .

items.title: Lies of P publisher files trademark for likely sequel 'Wonders of O'
items.summary: Sure sounds like a sequel to me.

content.v: First reported by Phrasemaker , Lies of P publisher Neowiz has filed an EU trademark for something called "Wonders of O" categorized as, among other, similar things, a bit of "virtual reality game software." While not 100% confirmed, there's a strong possibility that this is the Lies of P sequel we know is in development.

Similarly, it's difficult to see it being anything other than a Wizard of Oz adaptation in the same way Lies of P was a sicko's souslike Pinocchio. The name aside, Lies of P's post-credits scene ended with a view of a woman in ruby slippers clicking her heels⁠—prepare yourself for the tragic Cowardly Lion boss fight now, it'll be easier that way.

It just feels right, don't it? They're both fairy tales published in the Victorian era⁠—1881 for P, 1900 for O⁠—and while defined in the popular imagination by later Hollywood golden age film adaptations, the original works are far weirder and more interesting than most people give them credit for.

It seems like the marketing machine is starting to heat up for The Wonders of O. A few weeks ago, Lies of P developer Nough, formerly Round 8, put out a mini documentary hyping up its name change and work on the Lies of P sequel. Back in 2023, PCG news writer Lincoln Carpenter liked Lies of P well enough in his 74% review , but at the end of last year, our colleague Harvey Randall expressed his excitement for the studio's next game based on the quality of Lies of P's Overture expansion .

items.title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls Director Apologizes for Rough PC Launch and Outlines Upcoming Balance Changes
items.summary: The director of Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls issued a statement apologizing for the game’s rough launch on PC

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/27/wolverinethumb-1787851191203.png
The director of Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls issued a statement apologizing for the game’s rough launch on PC and outlined upcoming balance adjustments based on the dev team’s findings.

Kazuto Sekine, director of Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, published this statement on Monday, September 14, both in a short post on social media as well as a longer, in-depth blog post on the game’s Steam page .

To start, Sekine apologized for Tokon’s glaring issues on PC when it first released, which were so rough that even massive fighting game streamer Maximilian Dood uninstalled the game during a live broadcast.

“Seeing the game’s content so positively received, with players enjoying the experience and feeling inspired to keep playing, has been a tremendous source of joy for the entire development team,” Sekine began.

“However, we also recognize that the launch period was impacted by stability issues on PC, and we sincerely apologize for the frustration this has caused our players. It was never our intention for players to be unable to enjoy the game as we envisioned, and we are currently making progress on improvements to the PC version so that everyone can enjoy the game to the fullest.”
He went on to outline a couple of areas the development team believes “need to be addressed,” which included reassessing input responses and concerns of overly-frequent assists and tags.

“We have observed that particular inputs, such as attacks from aerial dashes or Free Flight, would sometimes not register correctly or even at all,” he explained. “To address these issues, we intend to adjust the current input windows to ensure a smoother and more responsive gameplay experience.

“In the current state, there is a 6-frame input buffer when holding a button. However, we intend to adjust the way inputs are handled so that, in certain cases, the action will be performed even when the button is not held.”

When it comes to frequent assists and tags, Sekine admitted that the game was originally balanced with the goal of players constantly tagging their characters in and out of battle. In fact, he revealed that the current state of the game has exceeded their expectations in this regard, though they acknowledged concerns from the community that this might be happening too frequently.

Namely, this means the team is working on increasing the cooldown time for certain assists and switches to “allow us to maintain rushdown capabilities while also creating more time for phases of neutral play.” Sekine said the team is looking into implementing these changes in updates “as soon as possible.”

Changes to overall character balance, however, will be minimal. Sekine and the Tokon team believe that it’s too soon to make sweeping changes, as they are currently in a “discovery phase." Sekine said that it is “still too early to start modifying character traits,” especially since the changes to assists and tags will also impact gameplay.

Tōkon Warriors! Game Director Kazuto “Pachi” Sekine has a message to share with you about our future battle balance update plans for #MARVELTokon : Fighting Souls, and more. Read the full message here: https://t.co/aJsOiguYNj Thank you all for your continued passion, patience,… pic.twitter.com/tHw3ymla22

This is the latest statement from the Tokon team after producer Takeshi Yamanaka apologized for the game’s rough PC launch and admitted that it would be “extremely challenging” to regain players’ trust.

“Unfortunately, in the PC version of the game, there have been in-game issues experienced by many players, which we really apologise to the player base for all of these problems,” he said in an August interview with VGC.

Despite these difficulties, Tokon was well-received critically, with IGN scoring the game a nine out of 10. After Steam reviews stumbled , Arc System Works was quick to push an update that solved many issues for PC players, and has been regularly communicating with the fighting game community in the weeks since then, as evidenced by this latest blog post.

items.title: Forget GTA 6, I have brought GTA 5 closer to being the true greatest game of all time: Hulk – Ultimate Destruction
items.summary: Quit staring.

others.title: Guide: 50 Best GameCube Games Of All Time

content.v: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .

Here's some logic for you: Grand Theft Auto 6—fattened on its billions—cannot help but be the greatest game of all time. This I have gathered from the apocalyptic euphoria that surrounds its release. But GTA 6 is not out yet, and the greatest game of all time, currently, is The Incredible Hulk: Ultimate Destruction for the PlayStation 2, original Xbox, and GameCube.
Ergo, QED, post hoc ergo propter hoc, abracadabra: GTA 6 will basically be like The Incredible Hulk: Ultimate Destruction.

With that key fact in mind, and with the aim of continuing to transform Grand Theft Auto the fifth into a facsimile of GTA 6 (this time on PC), I have installed Superman V into GTA 5. Your heroes now have laser eyes (also cryo eyes, pulse eyes, solar flare eyes, and so on), super speed, freeze breath, the ability to fly, and X-ray vision—which so far as I can tell is a heat-haze effect that happens intermittently.
I have waved goodbye to guns, much like the protagonist of A Farewell To Arms, who also probably did that after learning he could set people on fire by staring at them.

It works alarmingly well. I can ignite passing cars with my heat vision, freeze cops where they stand, and subject Los Santos' now-roving ambient hit squads to the carcinogenic effects of sustained X-ray exposure. I can also fly, which sometimes works, and sometimes results in Franklin, Michael, or Trevor tumbling lazily but uncontrollably through the sky, like an airborne flower.

My only concern is that, at this point, I am rapidly running out of keys on my keyboard with which to activate the various mods I have installed. At time of writing, hitting any of my function keys will summon a pile-up of distinct mod menus: Enhanced Native Trainer, Menyoo, the one that controls giving people piggybacks , the one that controls summoning dogs . What if what breaks by the end of this thing is not GTA 5, but my ability to control it?

items.title: Marathon Delays Next Major Update, Puts Focus on PvE, and Moves Away from Seasonal Content Amidst Bungie Struggles
items.summary: Bungie's struggles grow more evident as Marathon undergoes more drastic changes, with a move away from seasona

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/05/26/marathonthumb-1779822629000.png
Bungie's struggles grow more evident as Marathon undergoes a handful of drastic changes, with a move away from seasonal content, a focus on PvE, and a significant delay for the game's next update.

Bungie confirmed today that Marathon's next major update, which was slated to release on September 22, will now arrive on December 8. This update will add permanent PvE content, a social space with a firing range, an experimental TDM mode, and much more. On October 6, the game will get a smaller update that resets progression and the in-game economy to prepare for an overhaul.

Bungie noted that it is also moving away from traditional seasonal content updates in order to give the team more time to work on new content. The studio has also been made aware of feedback with regards to keeping players hooked via more depth, variety, and stronger progression, and is actively working to implement changes to respond to that. All in all, it's clear that Bungie is trying its very best to save Marathon amidst major struggles.

Marathon failed to impress players when it launched earlier this year and has only sunk further in the last few months. To make matters worse, Bungie also killed support for its biggest game, Destiny 2, in order to focus more on Marathon . It was a controversial move, and so far, it doesn't seem to be paying off. A swath of players have already written off Marathon, and Bungie's attempt to change the game's identity by moving away from the extraction elements likely won't change minds.

The next big update will be launching just a few weeks after Grand Theft Auto 6 and about two months after the release of Modern Warfare 4, which will have its own expansive extraction component known as DMZ. It's unclear what's in store for the future of Bungie outside of updates to Marathon, as the studio doesn't have anything in full-blown, active production at the moment. Hopes for Destiny 3 were quashed earlier this summer when Bungie laid off a sizable number of developers who were working on Destiny 2 , as well.

items.title: How WoW Forever Handles Its Massive Set Of New Quests
items.summary: One of the big announcements at BlizzCon was WoW Forever , the next iteration of offering a classic-style WoW

content.v: One of the big announcements at BlizzCon was WoW Forever , the next iteration of offering a classic-style WoW experience. Blizzard is hoping to draw players back to the OG WoW in a number of ways, including with the introduction of 1,000+ new quests. GameSpot caught up with Blizzard senior game designer Josh Greenfield to discuss this, along with why the game's OG quests--from 22 years ago--still resonate today.

If Blizzard is adding 1,000 more quests to WoW with the update, how many does that bring the game up to in total? It's a tricky question to answer, Greenfield said, in part because some of WoW's original quests are "tracking quests," but if you're counting "actual playable quests," the game has around 3,000 to 3,500.

So with 1,000+ more added of actual playable quests, that's a significant increase. WoW Forever also adds four new zones, and each of these has between 50 and 200 quests, so that's where many will come from. Additionally, the existing zones have been "glowed up," with the Wetlands and Azshara, specifically, getting a "lot of new quests to round them out as zones."
"Every nook and cranny, you're going to find something, even from like level five ... onward, you're going to start seeing new stuff," Greenfield said.

Also in our interview, we asked how Blizzard came up with the inspirations for the 1,000 new quests, and if there might be a new version of The Green Hills of Stranglethorn, which is regarded as perhaps the game's worst quest.

Greenfield said that was "kind of a terrible quest," but it still has charm and remains memorable even to this day. A lot of the original WoW is full of similarly memorable and "super iconic" quests, Greenfield said, and Blizzard is keen to carry the torch forward with WoW Forever.

"I think a lot of those quests explored the world at a very like ground level, and they they told stories at a very like ground level, a very like relatable level. You know, 'I am not the hero, I am a hero, and I'm going on this adventure with my dented shield and rusty sword.' And, you know, like things like The Missing Diplomat and things like that, like being able to kind of jet-set around the world and talk to different people and learn more about the cultures of each of these different zones, and learn a mystery and try and unravel a mystery."

Greenfield teased that Blizzard might "help finish unraveling that mystery" in WoW Forever. He went on to say some of the original WoW's quests were dark and grim, and Blizzard is embracing that philosophy with a lot of the new quests.

"Even Zephyr Isle, it's in the sky, it's nice and bright, but it's the story once you get into it, it's not it's not all, you know, sunshine and rainbows up there. It can be a little little hard," he said.

WoW Forever releases on November 4. In addition to the new zones and quests, players can expected update class designs, revamped systems, visual and gameplay improvements, and an expanded list of race and class options.

Players can access WoW Forever via their existing WoW subscription. However, players can buy the $80 Warcraft Forever Collection to receive the new Skyborne race, beta access, and early name reservation for WoW Forever. The Collection also includes Warcraft III: Reforged and Warcraft III: Reforged Forsaken Kingdom

items.title: Crazy Taxi Gets Crazier With Crazy Ex-Girlfriend Writers For New Movie
items.summary: The Crazy Taxi franchise isn't just getting a brand-new game next year ; it's also getting a live-action movie

content.v: The Crazy Taxi franchise isn't just getting a brand-new game next year ; it's also getting a live-action movie. Netflix and Sega have announced a new partnership that will see a Crazy Taxi film coming to the streaming service in 2027. Dan Gregor and Doug Mand are penning the comedy's screenplay, after previously working together on Naked Gun (2025), Crazy Ex-Girlfriend, and How I Met Your Mother.

There's no director attached to the project, yet. However, Original Film's Neal H. Moritz and Toby Ascher are producing the Crazy Taxi movie, alongside Sonic the Hedgehog series producer Toru Nakahara. "This film is for anyone who's spent hours behind the wheel of a yellow cab on their Dreamcast, with the music cranked up, smashing through everything in sight just to make the next fare," said Moritz and Ascher in the Netflix press release .

The Netflix and Sega collaboration also includes a new Sonic animated show aimed at "an upper preschool audience," as well as a live-action movie based on Stranger Than Heaven . The latter is the newest game from developer RGG Studio--known for the Yakuza and Like A Dragon titles.

Meanwhile, it will be intriguing to see how much the Crazy Taxi movie ties into Crazy Taxi: World Tour. The new arcade racing game will feature lore this time , such as driver backstories for why they got behind the wheel in the first place.

Fascinatingly enough, Sega has been trying to get a Crazy Taxi movie out on the road for basically two decades. In fact, Superman and The Goonies director Richard Donner was attached to direct the adaptation at one point.

items.title: Diablo 5 Isn’t Reinventing The Combat Wheel, It’s Making It Spin Even Faster
items.summary: Combat has grown massively between each numbered Diablo game, and for Diablo 5 , Blizzard is aiming to once ag

content.v: Combat has grown massively between each numbered Diablo game, and for Diablo 5 , Blizzard is aiming to once again elevate those gameplay mechanics to new heights.

"Fundamentally, we're an isometric action-RPG, and we're not looking to shake that up with Diablo 5," executive producer Matt Zitterman said to GameSpot at BlizzCon 2026 . "We're looking to improve on it, evolve it, and we have some great, interesting ideas about how to make combat feel even more visceral, even more action-forward. Kind of continuing to build on the success of that fast combat that started in Diablo 3, improved in Diablo 4, and we want to take it even further in Diablo 5. That's really what we're focused on from a combat and gameplay perspective."
Zitterman added that Blizzard was also looking to the past for inspiration, picking the best elements from those games and building them into Diablo 5.

"Something we talk about a lot on the team is we want Diablo 5 to be a game that feels like it has elements for you, regardless of which Diablo game was your favorite," Zitterman said. "We talk a lot about itemization in the game. Clearly, there's some inspiration being taken from Diablo 2 there, but we're also looking at Diablo 4 and the successes we've had there, and pulling forward ideas from there as well as Diablo 3. I think for us, Diablo 5 represents this really special moment in the franchise's history where we get to look at the past and bring forward things that feel really familiar, but give them a fresh take."

Diablo 5 will launch in 2029 , and this time, Diablo has finally won. Set decades after the Lord of Terror successfully conquered Sanctuary, there's no safe harbor or stronghold to retreat to this time, as players have to keep on the move and recruit allies to their caravan of survivors.

Diablo 5 will also give players more character classes to choose from than ever before, including the Monk, Demon Hunter, and the all-new Plague Knight that is empowered by spreading disease and pestilence across the battlefield.

items.title: Overwatch’s Tracer Once Shot Lasers From Her Eyes, And It Could Happen Again
items.summary: If early iterations of characters had survived the development process, Tracer could have been a very differen

content.v: If early iterations of characters had survived the development process, Tracer could have been a very different Overwatch hero. Speaking to GameSpot at BlizzCon 2026 , game director Aaron Keller mentioned that he had been playing Overwatch since 2013, "since Tracer was shooting lasers out of her eyes."
When questioned about such a strange sequence of words, Keller explained that the bizarre version of Tracer came from the first days of Overwatch's engine development in late 2013.

"When we were creating the Overwatch engine, you know, so this is late 2013, the first day we got Tracer in we all ran around but we didn't actually have a projectile system yet," he added. "So when you would fire, just like straight out of her eyes, [it was] two red lines."

There weren't even any proper visual effects involved at that point. According to Keller, it was "literally two red lines," because the game was firing the weapon from the camera's position. "And so we had a blast running around, just shooting lasers at each others," he recalled.

While the laser-eyed Tracer was ultimately replaced by the pulse pistols players know today, the idea apparently hasn't been completely banished from Blizzard's considerations. When asked whether the team might ever bring back a hero capable of shooting lasers from their eyes, associate game director Alec Dawson responded positively.
"I think shooting lasers out of your eyes is pretty cool. Yeah, we can figure something out," he said.

If Overwatch can finally have Jetpack Cat flying around the map, it can certainly have its roster stretched to accommodate laser beam eyes. "I think the possibilities are endless," Dawson added. He also joked that GameSpot's Jessica Cogswell should take credit if a future hero suddenly starts firing lasers from their eyes.

So, while Blizzard hasn't announced a laser-eyed hero, the idea was explicitly floated around during our interview, and the developers certainly didn't seem opposed to it. And honestly, after a decade of Overwatch, a hero shooting lasers out of their face might still be one of the least strange things Blizzard could add.
Overwatch's next character is Doctrine , while two existing heroes are getting substantial reworks .

items.title: Ubisoft Has Delayed Rayman Legends Retold Just a Few Weeks Before Its Planned Release Date
items.summary: Ubisoft has delayed Rayman Legends Retold from October to December.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/06/02/rayman-legends-retold-blogroll-01-1780429942056.jpg
Ubisoft has delayed Rayman Legends Retold from October to December.

Ubisoft confirmed the news via a social post today, noting that although Rayman Legends Retold has gone gold and was due out October 1, it isn't quite ready for launch. The team is taking the extra time to polish the game for release, which is now set for December 3. Expect a new look next week on September 22.

This will push Rayman Legends Retold out of the blast zone of major, earthshattering releases like Gears of War, Call of Duty, and GTA 6. Of course, Rayman appeals to a whole different audience, so those games may not have impacted its release in the first place, but it does allow it to soak up a bit more attention. Placing it in the heart of the holiday season may also give it more visibility for potential gifts, but we'll have to see how it all shakes out.

Rayman Legends Retold was announced earlier this summer, and the first previews for it were quite glowing . It's a reimagining of the 2013 platformer Rayman Legends, adding all kinds of new content, gameplay features, new 3D graphics, and much more. It is, by and large, a new game that leans on elements from the original release. It is the first Rayman game in 13 years so there's hope from fans that if this performs well, the franchise will live on and continue to thrive.

Ubisoft has been on a kick of remakes this year, with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and now Rayman Legends Retold. The publisher was also supposed to release a remake of Prince of Persia: Sands of Time, but it was canceled after quality concerns and years of troubles . It seems likely that Ubisoft will continue to remake classic titles from its past following the success of Black Flag Resynced.

items.title: Someone made a copper gaming PC Frankensteined out of an old blowtorch and other assorted parts and is 'just going to let it tarnish over time'
items.summary: It lives!

content.v: There's being into PC hardware and then there's crafting a glorious custom loop. Every time I see the latter I'm hit with a pang of jealousy, and it's no different here with Old-Mate-Fetus' custom copper build on Reddit .
We highlighted a similarly impressive different custom copper PC a few months ago. This latest copper build looks a little more extravagant to my eyes, and I'm not sure which I prefer.
In the centre is an Alphacool Core RX 9070 XT cooling block. Presumably it is the Aorus Elite version , given the Redditor says the motherboard is a Gigabyte B650M Aurous Elite Wifi.
Here's the full list of components (with perhaps slight variations from the specific models linked, which I have added):
According to Old-Mate-Fetus, the build weighs close to 20 kg.

The most eye-catching part of the build for me, and what sets it apart from other copper builds I've seen, is that blowtorch. Reminiscent of one of those handheld oil drippers mechanics use, but with a glorious copper sheen, plus a bunch of pipes poking out of it. It makes the whole thing look very artsy.
In another comment, the Redditor says they're "just going to let it tarnish over time, i quite like the look."

You won't catch me repurposing old PSU cables and blowtorches for a PC build anytime soon, but it's cool to see someone with the guts doing so and sharing the result—not mention, then using it to play Overwatch, judging by the corner of the screen: good choice.

items.title: Live-Action Crazy Taxi Movie, New Sonic Animated Series, and Stranger Than Heaven Adaptation Heading to Netflix
items.summary: Netflix has announced three Sega video game adaptations: a live-action comedy Crazy Taxi movie, a new Sonic an

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/25/crazytaxiworldtourmultiplayertrailer-ign-blogroll1-1787687086660.jpg

Netflix has announced three Sega video game adaptations: a live-action comedy Crazy Taxi movie, a new Sonic animated series, and a live-action movie adaptation of RGG Studio's yet to be released Stranger Than Heaven .
The Crazy Taxi movie is described as ‘live-action comedy,' and the Stranger Than Heaven adaptation is 'live-action crime.’ The new Sonic animation is obviously for kids.

Crazy Taxi comes first. It’s written by Dan Gregor and Doug Mand, the duo behind the 2025 reboot of The Naked Gun. Neal H. Moritz, Toby Ascher, and Toru Nakahara, the producers behind the Sonic franchise, are on board to produce.

“Great games already have what every adaptation is chasing — characters people love, worlds they know by heart, and fandoms that show up,” commented Brandon Riegg, VP of Nonfiction and Transmedia at Netflix. “With Crazy Taxi, Sonic, and Stranger Than Heaven, we get to work across three completely different eras of Sega’s catalog, celebrating everything fans love, while introducing them to new audiences.”

Shuji Utsumi, President and COO of Sega, added: "We've watched Netflix take on stories across every kind of format and treat each one with real craft, and seeing that same dedication applied to Sonic, Crazy Taxi, and Stranger Than Heaven is something we at Sega are incredibly proud to be a part of. The fandoms of these games deserve storytelling that honors what makes each title special, and we know Netflix shares that commitment. This is just the start of what these titles can become."

Toru Nakahara, Head Producer at Sega, told fans to expect “something cute yet cool” for Sonic, something “hilariously crazy” for Crazy Taxi, and a “badass action drama” for Stranger Than Heaven. Moritz and Ascher said of Crazy Taxi: “This film is for anyone who’s spent hours behind the wheel of a yellow cab on their Dreamcast, with the music cranked up, smashing through everything in sight just to make the next fare.”
Here’s the official blurb on Sonic:
And here’s the official line on Stranger Than Heaven:

Netflix is all in on video game adaptations, and there’s a lot in the works. It’s got a live-action Assassin's Creed series, live-action Gears of War film, animated series adaptations based on Minecraft, Magic: The Gathering, and Clash of Clans, and Overcooked competition series; second seasons of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and Splinter Cell: Deathwatch; and the third and final season of Devil May Cry. At BlizzCon 2026 over the weekend, Blizzard announced a Diablo animated series for Netflix , with talks ongoing for adaptations of Overwatch and Warcraft.

items.title: YouTuber gets classic Tomb Raider running on a chip that sips a mere 1 W of power
items.summary: Who needs an RTX 5090, am I right?

content.v: Modern PC gaming may not be the most energy efficient hobby. Even as someone who would sooner play yesteryear's favourite over this month's shiniest new game, I dread to think just how much smaller my electricity bill might be if it wasn't for my gaming rig. Thankfully for retro gaming fiends, energy efficient hardware isn't hard to come by.

Case in point, hardware creator Alejandro Villegas Alonso shared a clip of classic Tomb Raider running from a low-power chip . The SoC in question is the ESP32-P4 microcontroller, a lightweight 32-bit RISC-V processor featuring two 400 MHz cores which sips a mere 1 watt of energy according to the data sheet (via Tom's Hardware ).

It's not the kind of chip that would usually be used for anything like gaming, rather more for simple tasks in embedded devices such as cameras—that makes it all the more impressive that Alonso has got Tomb Raider up and running on it. It's particularly appealing given you can pick one of these up for very little cash .

The chip is running a port of OpenLara, a version of the original Tomb Raider that can be played in your browser with unlocked FPS . This version recreates the classic game in an open source engine so, no, this isn't a teeny tiny original PlayStation emulator or anything like that. Alejandro Villegas Alonso explains via the project's GitHub that this port "runs the classic Tomb Raider 1 engine with software rendering, audio, and USB HID keyboard input on Espressif's latest RISC-V SoC."

The project uses the ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board specifically, which comes with both a seven-inch capacitive touch screen and even a camera module. This obviously pushes the project's total power budget a little higher than 1W, with the power use of even just the 1024 x 600 LCD screen quickly overshadowing what's being used by the chip at this board's heart.

Alonso writes that their Tomb Raider port features a "software RGB565 renderer at 320 x 240, hardware-scaled to 1024 x 600 via the [...] Pixel Processing Accelerator." As Croft crunches through snow in the YouTube short, you can hear stereo audio via an ES8311 codec. Game inputs are handled via a USB keyboard, though that feels borderline profane to a console interloper like me.

With some versions of this development board costing a little under $30 , it's not hard to see why ESP32 microcontrollers are such a popular choice for DIY hardware projects. Recently, we've seen similar SoCs used in a credit card sized computer , the ' world's worst USB drive ', plus this pocket-sized Game Boy emulator based on an ereader . Creativity knows no bounds, but I wouldn't be surprised if we saw a few more retro gamers begin to bring yesteryear's favourites back to life on similarly low-power hardware.

content.v: 在最新一期 tinyBuild Connect 发布会上，独立游戏发行商 tinyBuild 公布了多项新消息与新作，其中包括两款全新游戏：《巨蟹横行》，一款以巨型移动甲壳生物为基底的 Roguelite 城市建造游戏；以及 《Road to Jukai》，一款以日本偏远山区为背景、围绕夜间出租车驾驶展开的第一人称心理恐怖游戏。
巨蟹横行
https://image.gcores.com/a74e63099735ae4168f99a889148ea00-920-430.png
由广受好评的《王之凝视》开发团队 Hypnohead 打造的全新作品《巨蟹横行》是一款 Roguelite 城市建造游戏——你的城市将建立在巨型生物之上。选择你的八足坐骑和骑手，合并建筑、解锁升级，在末日废土中一路前行，不断改造你的城市。毕竟，在一只巨型螃蟹背上建城，空间可是相当有限，每一个决定都至关重要！
没有两只螃蟹会走上同一条路。每一局游戏都会带来不同的挑战与机遇，让你以全新的方式建设自己的城市。对于懂得驾驭这片废土的人来说，这里遍地都是机会。你会扩充军队、提升生产，还是专心让你的坐骑一路向前？玩家可以在一局局短暂的 Roguelite 流程中体验完整的策略乐趣：建造、战斗、杀出一条路，然后带着积累的经验重新开始。
核心特色
深度策略与短局体验
每座建筑都有独特形态：空间有限，每一步都要做出艰难抉择
选择你的坐骑与骑手：不同外壳，不同玩法
合并并升级建筑，寻找足以打破游戏平衡的强力组合
100+种单位：以汽油与仇恨为动力
选择险路，或稳妥前行：选择更轻松的路线稳步推进，或挑战更艰难的道路，承担更高风险以换取更丰厚的奖励
Road to Jukai
https://image.gcores.com/52e7bbe6c87fd811a89d344437db0f22-1420-799.png
由 Endflame 开发的《Road to Jukai》（前称《Silent Road》）是一款第一人称心理恐怖游戏。玩家将化身日本偏远地区的一名夜班出租车司机，驾驶自己的出租车，在被诡异森林包围的小镇之间接送乘客。专心看路，但也千万别放松警惕——日落后搭上车的乘客，可没一个看起来那么简单。
《Road to Jukai》现已开启全新试玩，并将于 2027 年登陆 Steam。
核心特色
亡者从未离去: 在这个充满悲剧与谜团的日本偏远地区，体验一段横跨六个夜晚、非线性展开的诡异故事。这里，亡者依然在彼岸呼唤。
夜班时光: 接载一个个古怪的乘客，而他们的故事与要求也在一夜比一夜更加诡异。做好准备，迎接踏入你出租车的每一个人——或者每一种“东西”。
盯紧前方的路: 驾车穿行于森林公路，往返于寂静的小镇之间，亲眼见证夜幕降临后发生的一切。只希望太阳能快点升起。

items.title: “黑影”改为辅助是正确的举动，但我担心一些《守望先锋》玩家可能需要时间来适应
items.summary: The Sombra hatred runs deep.

content.v: No one knows how to haunt the narrative quite like Overwatch's two misfits, Roadhog and Sombra. When these heroes are strong the game sucks for everyone else, but when they're nerfed for the sake of everyone else there's almost no reason to play them. This has meant that both characters are in a perpetual state of buff/nerf; it's tough out here to be a hog.

So it comes as absolutely no surprise that the two characters picked to undergo yet another redesign over at Blizzcon were the dynamic duo Hog and Sombra. But it wouldn't be an Overwatch balance change without at least a little bit of upset.

A new Support Hero is here and we don't just mean Doctrine 👾Get your first look at Sombra and Roadhog’s new reworked kits before trying them out in Season 5. pic.twitter.com/vGGf5Lm32h September 12, 2026
Hog's new look seems sound enough—especially with the much-needed addition of Trash Compactor which works as a de facto shield. But Sombra's change to the Support role has players up in arms.
Much of Sombra's previous kit has stayed the same, with her primary fire, EMP ult, and translocator ability all left intact. But she also has two new abilities and passives:
Change can be difficult, but I actually like this new look.

Sure it's annoying that Sombra can't hack heroes out of their ult, but she still has EMP for that. And it'll be frustrating for flanker DPS mains that they now have one less hero to use against Widowmaker, but Tracer can get that job done. If used correctly, I think this can turn Sombra from an outlier to a standard pick.

There's only one issue: Overwatch players are stubborn as all hell.. First up, Overwatch players don't like playing against Sombra, and her ban rates in competitive are ingrained into the psyche of some players, so I don't think this restyle will help change her public image all that much at first.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4ZQDpvxuLEUfQUt5TeKsBd-1920-80.jpg

Then there's the fact that in all likelihood a great deal of players will play Sombra in her old fashion as a flanker, instead of a support who's new role is to stick with her team and tank. If there's one thing that pisses me off it's support players who justify DPS joyrides as another way to support their team.

If you're not in Masters or above then that just isn't true. While healing isn't the whole role of a support, there's facilitating engagement and boosting ally's kill-potential, the main goal of a support should always be self and team sustain. So having one support off on the other side of the map spawn camping the enemy team's Mercy will probably be a commonly frustrating experience.

But these issues are just growing pains. I'm sure overtime Sombra's new role will settle itself into the muscle memory of players. I have a feeling she'll become a valued member of her new role much like Doomfist and Symmetra.

items.title: The Triple-I Initiative Showcase Is Getting A Second Event In 2026
items.summary: The Triple-I Initiative Showcase is officially coming back on October 8 at 9 AM PT / 12 PM ET , and this secon

content.v: The Triple-I Initiative Showcase is officially coming back on October 8 at 9 AM PT / 12 PM ET , and this second instalment of the show will once again offer plenty of trailers and announcements from a wide variety of publishers and developers. Since the first presentation kicked off in 2024, the Triple-I Initiative has been an annual event, but the organizers say they have even more to show next month with a second dose of back-to-back video game trailers.

Viewers can expect eight exclusive world premieres from studios such as Team17, Amanita Design, Strange Scaffold, and Norsfell, as well as reveals for Dave the Diver, Brotato, Chained Together, Risk of Rain 2, and Windrose. The showcase will run for around 45 minutes, and there'll also be news for games like Hela: of Mice and Magic, Militsioner, the new Among Us title, Pony Island 2: Panda Circus, Haunted Paws, and Outward 2.
As usual, you can catch it live through the Triple-I Initiative's usual channels, like YouTube and Twitch .

The April showcase was a pretty impressive one from the Triple-I Initiative, as it featured back-to-back trailers for Risk of Rain 2 DLC, a darkly creative typing game called Final Sentence, and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. As with several other video game showcases, the Triple-I Initiative has adopted a format that focuses purely on game trailers, with no adverts or sponsors wedged between them.

Organized by Evil Empire--the developers behind the new Castlevania game that's out in October--the presentation is designed to offer high visibility for a curated selection of games from various creative teams.
